Definition: from the same as G1201; (passively) a captive:--prisoner.
BiblicalUsage: This is the word for a prisoner, and Luke uses it for Paul's companions on the voyage to Rome. They sail with him as prisoners, and when the ship breaks apart the soldiers plan to kill them lest any escape.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Luke names the prisoners because he was there; the voyage to Rome was not a story told at second hand; it was a storm survived with chained men aboard, and Paul's calm in it is the witness.
